summary: These tables cover institutions reporting enrollment and instructional activity during July 1, 2021–June 30, 2022, using annual 12-month measures rather than a single-term snapshot. The universe is participating IPEDS institutions with undergraduate and/or graduate activity; headcounts are unduplicated across the period, while instructional activity is reported as credit and/or contact hours. The survey is especially useful for institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs, but the measures should not be interpreted as term-specific enrollment.

The Completions component covers awards granted and programs offered during July 1, 2021–June 30, 2022, reported by institutions in the IPEDS postsecondary completions universe. It describes institution-level completions and program offerings, with records further divided by program, award level, demographic characteristics, or distance-education status depending on the table. No even/odd-year reporting restriction applies to these 2022 data; award-level categories and detailed distance-education information introduced in 2019–20 are available.

Fall Enrollment covers students enrolled at eligible postsecondary institutions during the fall reporting period. Traditional academic-year institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The unit of observation is the institution, with tables generally containing multiple institution-level records defined by the applicable breakdown fields; the survey’s universe is participating IPEDS institutions reporting eligible postsecondary enrollment.

The Finance survey is collected annually during the winter collection period and reports institution-level financial information for the most recently completed fiscal year, using the institution’s applicable accounting standards. Its universe is active, Title IV-eligible postsecondary institutions required to report to IPEDS, with one institutional record per applicable finance form. Across the survey, fiscal year 2020 and later scholarship and fellowship amounts include discounts and allowances by source; since fiscal year 2016, detailed expenditures by function and certain natural classifications are no longer collected, while financial-health measures and expanded endowment data were added where applicable.

The 2022 Graduation Rates component is an annual institution-level collection reporting the status of eligible full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts as of August 31, 2022. Its universe is IPEDS institutions with such undergraduate cohorts, with reporting organized by institution, cohort, and outcome status; the applicable cohort year and institution sector vary by table. The component covers completion and transfer outcomes within specified percentages of normal time, with some supplemental tables limited to particular institution types or financial-aid and gender subcohorts.

These Human Resources tables cover institution-reported staff on the payroll as of November 1, 2022, salary and outlay information for the 2022-23 academic year, and full-time permanent new hires from November 1, 2021, through October 31, 2022. The unit is an institution-level staff or new-hire record, with multiple records per institution when staff are classified by occupational, rank, tenure, demographic, or other categories. Tables marked for degree-granting institutions are limited to institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016.

Institutional Characteristics covers institution-level reporting for the 2022-23 IPEDS universe, collected primarily in the fall, with selected admissions-related fields updated from the winter admissions collection. Reporting is generally required for active institutions participating in Title IV federal financial aid programs; records may also identify nonresponse, imputation, applicability, and parent/child multi-campus reporting. Most records describe institutions, although the branch-campus file uses reported campus locations and the comparison-group file lists institutions selected for custom groups.

These tables report institution-level student financial aid information for the July 1, 2021–June 30, 2022 academic year, using students enrolled or receiving assistance during that period as the reporting populations. The universe is participating IPEDS postsecondary institutions eligible to report student financial aid data; populations and measures vary by table, including undergraduate, graduate, degree-seeking, and benefit-recipient groups. The survey covers aid counts and dollars awarded or received, rather than institutional finances or student-level records.
